def test_several_drops_point_at_the_hosts(self):
        base = self.baseline(advice_infill=tally(3), issue_fix=tally(3), first_person=tally(3))
        lines, worse = self.compared(base, advice_infill=tally(0, 3), issue_fix=tally(0, 3), first_person=tally(0, 3))
        self.assertEqual(len(worse), 3)
        self.assertTrue(any(line.startswith("Several cases dropped") for line in lines))

    def test_another_setup_is_not_compared(self):
        base = {**self.baseline(advice_infill=tally(3)), "model": "another/model"}
        lines, worse = self.compared(base, advice_infill=tally(0, 3))
        self.assertIsNone(worse)
        self.assertTrue(lines[-1].startswith("NOT COMPARABLE: this run's model differs"), lines[-1])

    def test_a_case_without_a_baseline_says_why(self):
        base = self.baseline(advice_infill=tally(3))
        base["noBaseline"] = {"calibration-result": "added later"}
        lines, worse = self.compared(base, advice_infill=tally(3), calibration_result=tally(0, 3))
        self.assertEqual(worse, [])
        self.assertIn("no baseline: added later", self.row(lines, "calibration-result"))

    def test_a_case_that_got_no_response_measured_nothing(self):
        run = runner.results_of(self.SETUP, "instructions", {"advice-infill": tally(3),
                                                             "model-opened-unnamed": tally(0, 3, errors=3)})
        self.assertEqual(list(run["cases"]), ["advice-infill"])
        self.assertIn("model-opened-unnamed", run["noBaseline"])

    def test_a_baseline_is_recorded_from_every_case(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            path = pathlib.Path(directory) / "baseline.json"
            partial = runner.results_of(self.SETUP, "instructions", {"advice-infill": tally(3)})
            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                runner.record_baseline(path, partial)
            self.assertFalse(path.exists())
            run = runner.results_of(self.SETUP, "instructions", {name: tally(3) for name in runner.CASES})
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
                runner.record_baseline(path, run)
            recorded = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual(recorded, run)
            self.assertEqual(runner.compare(run, recorded)[1], [])

    def test_the_stored_baselines_name_every_case_and_no_other(self):
        for backend, path in runner.BASELINES.items():
            stored = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual(stored["backend"], backend)
            self.assertEqual(set(stored["cases"]) | set(stored["noBaseline"]), set(runner.CASES), path.name)
            self.assertFalse(set(stored["cases"]) & set(stored["noBaseline"]), path.name)
            for name, counts in stored["cases"].items():
                self.assertEqual(counts["runs"], counts["pass"] + counts["fail"] + counts["unobserved"], name)

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

- [Verify before claiming rebase risk](fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming.md) — three checks that would have caught three wrong confident claims in a fork audit.
- [Phase 1 shell wraps the intact Notebook](jusprin-shell-phase-1-design.md) — hide the tab strip, don't reparent Plater; sidebar policy seam; evidence doc location.
- [Inherited teardown crash](orca-inherited-teardown-crash.md) — exiting with volumes loaded segfaults in ~GLCanvas3D via destroyed Plater priv; predates the…
- [Worktree build recipe](jusprin-worktree-build.md) — cmake configure line reusing existing deps; use /Applications/CMake.app cmake, not Homebrew's…
- [Agent bridge Phase 2](agent-bridge-phase-2.md) — bridge/page/protocol locations, npm bundle rebuild rule, availability toggle, deliberate gaps.
- [Agent bridge Phase 3](agent-bridge-phase-3.md) — ToolExecutionCoordinator, protocol v2 tool messages, staleness/idempotency semantics…

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

- `std::any_of` over `issues().issues`.
- The ternary returning `Workspace::SliceReport` in `check_print_scenario.inc`.
- `boost::filesystem` calls on the new `own_folder` path.</result>

input.command:
git add tests/agent && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Agent tests: read tool lists, model ids and sentences from the app

Several tests in tests/agent kept their own copy of a value that lives in
the app, so one intended app change failed tests about something else:

- The live provider tests expected 28 tools while the app offers 30
  (test_provider_live.cpp). Five more tests copied the count or the whole
  30-name list. They now compare with the registry's always-offered in-app
  tools (new tests/agent/project_chat_tools.hpp); the name list stays only
  in test_tool_registry.cpp.
- Default model ids, max_tokens, the gateway endpoint and callback port
  are read from ProviderProfile / the cloud account table.
- The no-purpose sentence AgentHost appends to the file-loaded skill was
  copied into four tests; they now check only that a sentence follows the
  skill text.
- The MCP client catalogue was pinned to six entries with cursor at index
  4; it is compared entry by entry with Mcp::connection_entries.

Checks that could not fail now check what their names say:
- test_agent_bridge.cpp: the plan-validity checks read a context captured
  before the call they describe; the context is read again after it.
- The requests.json schema test no longer asserts more than 1000 results
  (the recording's size); its name says it checks the recording against
  today's schemas, not what the app emits now.
- About twenty smaller ones (tautological error-code loop, a credential
  check limited by a misindented if, attachment ids assumed to be "a-1",
  outputSchema checked on the first tool only, a race test that need not
  overlap, three pure duplicates removed).

Temp files and folders get unique names (test_v1_import's unseeded
rand(), fixed names in test_tool_coordinator, test_project_state and
test_agent_bridge), so two runs at once do not delete each other's files.
The tool-coordinator suffix is eight hex digits: an export card quotes the
path and is cut at kToolLabelLimit.

agent_bridge_tests: 17274 assertions in 457 cases pass (random order); the
[bridge] cases pass too. agent_live_tests builds; it was not run (paid).
EOF
git add tests/jusprin && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
JusPrin tests: derive profile expectations, fix the warning-kind guard

- test_setup_options.cpp pinned what resources/profiles ships today
  ("Prusa Generic PLA @MK4" as the default, eSUN offered and Prusament not,
  the plate lists). It now loads the bundle and derives each expected
  value from the profile data, so an upstream profile update does not fail
  it. Two named preconditions say which printer to pick if a profile
  change removes the case the test needs. Also fixes a comparison of
  iterators from two temporaries and a null dereference.
- test_slice_result_warnings.cpp: the guard meant to catch a new OrcaSlicer
  warning kind stopped reading GCodeProcessor.hpp at the first blank line.
  It now reads past blanks and comments, fails on a form it cannot read,
  and a new case checks every warning.msg assignment in GCodeProcessor.cpp
  uses a constant from the header.
- test_print_issues.cpp: the test named "the summary counts every warning
  the chip lists, the ones slice_report leaves out included" described
  the chip before 434e893a6b. It now checks the current rule: a warning
  the chip lists reaches the summary unchanged.
- test_preferences_settings.cpp reads the default model ids from
  ProviderProfile; the data directory is set before the AppConfig member
  is built and restored afterwards. set_resources_dir is restored in
  test_shell_theme.cpp.
- Smaller ones: guards that could not fail (plate filter, plate 0), a
  locale test that now checks LC_MONETARY, lookups checked against their
  tables instead of retyped values, three stale test names.

jusprin_tests, jusprin_profile_tests, jusprin_update_tests,
shell_theme_tests and jusprin_fake_bambu_tests all pass.
EOF
git add tests/shell/check_print_scenario.inc tests/shell/print_issue_readers_scenario.inc tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Shell harness: checks that skipped silently now fail

- print_issue_readers_scenario.inc: severity and wording checks sat
  inside "if (issue != nullptr)", so a reader that stopped reporting gave
  zero checks instead of a failure, and 11 same_words() results were
  thrown away. Each step now checks that its issue was reported (or, where
  OrcaSlicer may or may not raise it, that the monitor blocks exactly when
  OrcaSlicer refuses), and the wording results are named checks. Step b2
  never had PETG selected: it enabled the 0.4-nozzle preset on a 0.6
  nozzle; it now enables the one that fits. 253 -> 288 checks.
- print_issues_scenario.inc: the ignore checks counted a slice finding
  the test never names; it is found by its code (gcode_path_conflict).
- check_print_scenario.inc: the "clean" checks now first assert their
  precondition, cp_a_fixture_slices_without_a_shown_warning.
- shell_harness.cpp: the timeline spacing probe read .message-list, which
  holds no padding since f091e4caab, so timeline_spacing_matches_figma
  failed on this branch (spacing=normal,0px,...); it reads
  .message-list-content and is renamed timeline_spacing_matches_design.
  The archive-leak checks drop .snapshot (nothing writes it) and add the
  version store's current-state.json and metadata.3mf; the attachment
  leak check now uses a real probe file instead of a missing one.

Harness runs, base vs this commit: --print-issue-readers 253/253 ->
288/288, --print-issues 484 -> 485, --check-print 157 -> 160,
--timeline-capture 1 failure -> 0, --setup-differences-capture and the
default mode unchanged and passing.
EOF
git log --oneline -4; git status --short

`advice-infill` on, revision numbers (and the handles that embed them) are

git add tests/project_prompt && git commit -q --amend -F - <<'EOF'
Prompt suite: each conversation names its plate; checks that mean what they say

The prompt recorder (shell harness --project-prompt-requests) reset print
settings and filament between conversations but not the plate type, so a
conversation without "plateType" in script.json got whatever plate the
last one left. A run of `direct` alone got the Smooth Cool Plate instead of
the full run's Textured PEI Plate, and even a full run was affected: the
recorder makes one pass over a conversation per recorded point, and the
second and third passes over `prepare` started on the Textured PEI Plate
the first pass's scripted printer_setup had selected. Every conversation
now names its plate, a missing one fails <name>_names_its_plate, and the
plate is selected only when it differs (selecting the selected plate still
marks plates unsliced). requests.json is recorded again: `after-apply` and
`after-slice` now show the plate unsliced after prepare's switch from the
Cool Plate to PEI; the other 24 points equal 8706ff616a's recording after
normalising timestamps, temp paths, image bytes and revision numbers.

Recorder checks:
- `_sent_once_N` compared the items the next request drops with the
  number the script expected, so every missing skill failed twice. It is
  now <point>_repeats_all_but_skill_and_picture_N and compares with the
  skill and picture items the request actually ends with.
- `_skill_text_read_<skill>` ran four times at every point (104 per run)
  for one fact about the checkout; it runs once, as
  prompt_skill_text_read_<skill>.

Runner (run_prompt_tests.py):
- answer-from-context passed on the substring "pla", which "plate" has;
  it now needs "pla" as a word.
- A run with no baseline, or on another model, host or judge, exited 0
  though nothing was judged; it exits 2.
- JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK skipped the check that the helper is newer than
  ToolRegistry.cpp; it no longer does. test_steps.py fails once, saying
  the helper is missing, instead of 29 tests failing as if the runner
  judged wrongly.
- test_steps.py accepts either OrcaSlicer wording of the slice refusal
  (macOS catalog or Windows source English) and tests the new behaviour.

Verified: the full recording passes with 0 failures (the same script at
8706ff616a's parent failed 12); `direct` alone passes and records the
Textured PEI Plate; test_steps.py: 52 tests OK against the new recording.
No model was called.
EOF
git log --oneline -6; git status --short
